lines.en: My brown wings hug the bark
I climb the trunk in flight
I skim the heap of rotting leaves
I fly low along the bank
I pass through vine shadow
I beat once and glide
I wheel about the flowers
I make for a gap in the grove
I fly close to the earth
I come out from under a leaf
I ride the warmth upward
I cut diagonally through brush
I fly down along a dry branch
I skim the moss on a stone
I pass between blades of grass
I fly toward the roots
I rest on a dead log
My brown wings are shut tight
I stay in the shade
My markings look like bark
I wait for a breeze
I rest on bare earth
My antennae sway lightly
I listen to the undergrowth
I am easy to miss, and that suits me
I slowly change my stance
My wing edges are worn smooth
I cling to the back of a flower
I look up from the bark
You have come near these blooms
I fold my wings to hide
You will not easily see me

lines.zh: 我在树皮上换了个角度
lines.en: I shift my angle on the bark
Your shadow sweeps the bark
I look up at your face
You crouch to look at the flowers
My color matches the woods
I slip to the other side of the trunk
I tumble onto a leaf
My wing is pressed out of shape
I pause on the bark
A small flake of scale dust is gone
My beats come uneven
I hide under a leaf
I take my time getting up
That didn't snap my wing
That dazed me for a while
I rest against the trunk
That is a red bloom
I smell something familiar
You turn it toward me
I settle on it and try
There is not much nectar in this one
I walk around the petal rim
I put my proboscis in
This one is a bit past its prime
I would rather have a fresh one
I will fly once I am done
You knocked off some scales
I bump against the trunk
I drop onto a leaf
I press myself to the bark
Your heel lands beside me
One wing is bent
I steady myself in the air
I drop behind the leaf to hide
That gave me a fright
I open my wings again
There are other brown wings here
I follow the scent to them
He rests on the same flowers
We circle a trunk together
I settle just above him
We do not fight over the bloom
Our colors are almost the same
Two more brown shadows join the grove
One then the other, quietly
And we part again
I crawl onto the thing
It is rough as bark
My foreleg taps it
No petal is this hard
I fly off and land back
I took it for a leaf
I rest on it a moment
Not a trace of nectar sweetness
I go back to the flowers
I circle once around it
I have found a red bloom
I fly over that way
That bloom is in the understory
I chase it through vine shadow
I hold myself very low
I am picking my landing
I switch to another bloom
I go up the trunk
I am almost there
I dive toward that red
I ease toward the petals
The bloom is still swaying
I wait for it to settle
I narrow my wings
I come around the leaf's back
This bloom is set too high
I drop a little lower
This petal is rather slick
I try another landing angle
I am close to the flower's heart
My wing sweeps your finger
I knock your hand's back
I beat upward and burst away
My wing tip brushes you
I wheel about your wrist
I beat my wings loudly
I did not dodge that one
I return to the bark
I flap about wildly
I flick you with my wing edge
A patch of brown joins the bark
I come out of a crack in the log
My wings open under the trees
I settle on a red bloom
I fly out of the vine shadow
I rise from just above the ground
A brown butterfly joins the understory
I steady myself with slow beats
I round a broken branch
My shadow falls on dead leaves
Flame scalds my wing corner
I land in the leaf litter
Water weighs my wings down
The blast lifts the dead leaves
An arrowhead shaves a corner off my wing
Magic flares across my markings
Fewer blooms, and I fly faint
The flash makes me flinch
I keep falling into the dark
